--- title: "Genome browser tracks in R with canvasXpress" description: "Stack coverage and gene-model tracks over genomic coordinates in R — an interactive, zoomable browser view from one portable spec." author: "Isaac Neuhaus" date: "2026-10-29" categories: [R, canvasXpress, genome, bioinformatics, visualization] image: "thumbnail.png" --- A genome browser view stacks **tracks** that share one coordinate axis: coverage, gene models, variants. In R this usually means `Gviz` or `ggbio`. Here we build an interactive, zoomable view with [canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org) — and the whole thing is one portable spec. ## The data shape A Genome figure is a list of **tracks** that share one coordinate axis — each with a `type`. Real browser views stack several: here we build four — **gene models** (`box`, multi-exon, connected), **coverage across three tissues** (`bar`), an **expression heatmap** (`heatmap`), and **variant markers** (`triangle`). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(canvasXpress) set.seed(3) # Gene models: each gene is a set of exon [start, end] intervals, drawn connected. genes <- lapply(0:3, function(j) { start <- 40 + j * 120 exons <- lapply(0:(sample(2:4, 1) - 1), function(k) list(start + k * 30, start + k * 30 + 18)) list(id = paste0("GENE", j + 1), dir = if (j %% 2 == 0) "right" else "left", fill = "rgb(70,130,220)", outline = "rgb(0,0,0)", data = exons) }) # Coverage and expression: one entry per binned position, three tissues each. offsets <- 50 + (0:21) * 22 coverage <- lapply(seq_along(offsets), function(i) list(id = paste0("p", i), offset = offsets[i], data = list(sample(8:45, 1), sample(8:45, 1), sample(8:45, 1)))) express <- lapply(seq_along(offsets), function(i) list(id = paste0("p", i), offset = offsets[i], data = list(round(rnorm(1), 2), round(rnorm(1), 2), round(rnorm(1), 2)))) # Variants: point markers at genomic positions. snps <- lapply(0:8, function(k) list(id = paste0("rs", 1000 + k), offset = sample(45:520, 1), fill = "rgb(200,40,40)", outline = "rgb(0,0,0)")) genome <- list(tracks = list( list(name = "Genes (exon models)", type = "box", connect = TRUE, data = genes), list(name = "Coverage — Heart / Liver / Kidney", type = "bar", height = 120, fill = "rgb(80,80,200)", outline = "rgb(60,60,60)", data = coverage), list(name = "Expression (z-score)", type = "heatmap", height = 90, data = express), list(name = "SNPs", type = "triangle", data = snps) )) ``` ::: ## The plot The Genome graph type is passed through to the engine as-is; `featureStaggered` spreads crowded features so labels stay legible. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} canvasXpress( data = genome, graphType = "Genome", background = "rgb(245,245,245)", featureStaggered = TRUE, title = "Multi-track genome browser: genes, coverage, expression and variants", width = 760, height = 520 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` The Genome graphType is an advanced chart, data is passed as-is to the JS library ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Scroll/drag to pan and zoom into a region; every track stays locked to the shared coordinate axis, so the gene models, coverage, expression and variants line up position-for-position. Swap each track for your own pileup, annotation and VCF-derived data. ## Why "reproducible" The tracks and `config` **are** the figure — one portable spec that renders the identical browser view from Python or JavaScript, and can be validated and re-rendered later. ## Next - [Interactive network graphs in R](../network-graphs-in-r/) - Gallery: - Package:
